## Final review: security, diff-only (45de0559..9456958b; labelled round 6 in the main transcript)

- Source: `<transcripts>/148019cc-de64-4bee-8c80-932a311792cc/subagents/agent-ab02673554b3e1e4c.jsonl` (final assistant message)
- Timestamp: 2026-10-30T14:35:59.376Z

## Security Review Findings
### P1 — Critical Security Issues (Blocks Merge)
| **SEC-1 · security · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:2162`** (also `:1579`, `lib/command-parse.sh:714,762-788`)<br>**Shells fed by a pipe without being right after it no longer ask.** The tier gate now asks about a shell reading its input only when the `__BD_PIPE__` mark is set. That mark goes on the first simple command after `\|` and is cleared on output. Every new `(`, `$(` or backquote level starts unmarked. When the right side of a pipe is a group, loop or subshell, the shell inside it is not the first command, and a process substitution has no `\|` at all. All of these are silent now and asked at 45de0559:<br>`echo 'gh pr merge 7' \| { :; bash; }`<br>`echo 'gh pr merge 7' \| ( :; bash )`<br>`echo 'gh pr merge 7' \| (bash)`<br>`echo 'gh pr merge 7' \| if true; then bash; fi`<br>`printf 'x\ngh pr merge 7\n' \| { read -r _; bash; }`<br>`echo 'gh pr merge 7' > >(bash)`<br>`echo 'gh pr merge 7' \| tee >(bash)`<br>`echo 'git push origin --delete v1' \| { :; bash; }`<br>I ran each shape for real with `echo HIT` in place of the merge, in both bash and zsh, and the inner `bash` executed the line every time. _(HIGH)_ | The pipe mark applies to a whole pipeline element, not one simple command. Keep it set until the element ends (the matching `}`, `)`, `fi`, `done`, or the next `;`/`&&`/newline at depth 0), and carry it into a `(` level. Treat a shell inside `>(...)` or `<(...)` as fed. The safer default is the old one: ask for every shell that reads standard input, and exempt only a shell that is provably not fed (a bare `which bash` with no pipe or process substitution anywhere in the command). Add every command above as a must-ask row. |
| **SEC-2 · security · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:1542`** (`lib/command-parse.sh` awk `qs`)<br>**A quoted array or positional expansion used as the command is exempted.** `TOKQ=1` marks any word that is one quoted string. The command-word check then skips the "command held in a variable" ask. But `"${A[@]}"`, `"$@"` and `"${A[@]:0}"` expand to several words, so they run a whole command. Silent now, asked at 45de0559:<br>`A=(gh pr); A+=(merge 7); command "${A[@]}"`<br>`A=(gh pr); A+=(merge 7); X=1 "${A[@]}"`<br>`A=(gh pr); A+=(merge 7); sudo "${A[@]}"`<br>`A=(gh pr); A+=(merge 7); command "${A[@]:0}"`<br>`set -- gh pr; set -- "$@" merge 7; X=1 "$@"`<br>I ran the `echo HIT` equivalents and they execute. The old exemption checked whether the segment text started with a quote, so it covered only the bare form. _(HIGH)_ | Do not set `qs` (or do not honour `TOKQ`) when the quoted word contains `$@`, `${@`, or `${NAME[@]` (including slices). `"$*"` and `"${A[*]}"` really are one word, so they can stay exempt. Add the five commands above as must-ask rows. |
| **SEC-3 · security · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:1823`** (also `:1821`)<br>**Renaming a branch now lets a same-named tag be pushed.** `git branch -m/-M/-c/-C` (and `--move/--copy`) now set `up=1` instead of `hit=1`. So a later push that names both a remote and a refspec no longer asks. That push's refspec is still checked against the branch list as it was before the command ran. Silent now, asked at 45de0559:<br>`git branch -m feat tmp && git tag feat && git push origin feat`<br>`git branch -m tmp && git tag feat && git push origin feat`<br>I ran this against a local bare repository: the remote received `refs/tags/feat`, a tag push with no prompt. The rename is what makes it work: with both branch and tag named `feat`, git refuses the push as ambiguous. _(HIGH)_ | Move `m/M/c/C` and `--move/--copy` back to `hit=1`, or set the "pushes ask" flag when one appears: a branch rename or copy changes which names are local branches, not just upstream keys. Keep `up=1` for `-u/--set-upstream-to/--unset-upstream/-t/--track`. Add the command above as a must-ask row. |
| **SEC-4 · security · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/lib/command-parse.sh:258`** (and the `*'${'*` fast-path guard in `_bd_words`)<br>**An unquoted `${...}` containing spaces is read as one word.** `_bd_words` now reads `${...}` as one word, spaces included. Unquoted, bash splits it into several words (checked: `${X:- -rf}` → `[-rf]`, `${X:-gh pr merge 7}` → `[gh][pr][merge][7]`). The destructive-command hook used to see the split-off pieces and now does not. Allowed now, blocked (exit 2) at 45de0559:<br>`rm ${X:- -rf} /tmp/zz`<br>`rm ${X:- -r -f} /tmp/zz`<br>`git clean ${X:- -f}`<br>`git clean ${X:- -fdx} .`<br>`git branch ${X:- -D} feat`<br>The tier gate is silent on all of them, so nothing stops them. In the unchecked-merge hook, `${X:-gh pr merge 7}` is now allowed (exit 0, blocked at 45de0559); the tier gate still asks on that one, so it is not silent overall. _(HIGH)_ | For a word that is an unquoted `${...}` holding whitespace, add a second reading split on that whitespace, as the substitution second reading does, or mark the word unreadable so every hook treats it as possibly anything. Keep it one word only when it is inside double quotes. Add the commands above as must-block and must-refuse rows. |
### P2 — Security Concerns
### P3 — Security Improvements
| **SEC-5 · security · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:1542`**<br>Already present at 45de0559: `A=(gh pr); A+=(merge 7); "${A[@]}"`, with the quoted array as the first word, is silent on both trees because of the old "segment starts with a quote" exemption. _(HIGH)_ | Fixed by the same change as SEC-2. |
| **SEC-6 · security · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/lib/command-parse.sh`** (`_BD_SHELLS`)<br>Already present at 45de0559: `CMD="gh pr merge 7"; tcsh <<EOF` / `$CMD` / `EOF` and the same with `fish` are silent on both trees. `tcsh`, `csh`, `fish`, `yash` and `rbash` are not in the shell list, so the heredoc reader check treats them as data readers. _(HIGH)_ | Add them to `_BD_SHELLS`. |
| **SEC-7 · security · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/lib/command-parse.sh`** (`_bd_expand_interpreter_args`, piped pass)<br>Already present at 45de0559: `echo 'git reset --hard' \| { :; bash; }` gets past the destructive-command hook on both trees. The quoted words are read only from the segment immediately before the shell. Same cause as SEC-1. _(HIGH)_ | Fix together with SEC-1. |
| **SEC-8 · security · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/block-destructive.sh`**<br>Already present at 45de0559: `git reset ${X:---hard}`, `git reset ${X:-HEAD --hard}` and `${X:-git reset --hard}` get past both trees. _(HIGH)_ | The fix for SEC-4 covers the spaced forms. For `${X:---hard}`, read the default text as a possible word. |

## Final review: code, diff-only (45de0559..9456958b)

## Code Review Findings: 45de0559..9456958b (HEAD 9456958ba4a791b429f0886cb3a5e665a87930bc, unchanged during the review)
I found one P1 and three P2s, so the recommendation is **REQUEST_CHANGES**. All five allowed test files pass at 9456958b (exit 0 each; e2e-tier-gate 2920 pass, 0 fail), and none of them includes the shapes below.
**How each finding was reproduced.** The probe script `<scratch>` feeds each command to all three hooks in two trees: the code at 45de0559 ("old") and at 9456958b ("new"). It uses a scratch repo on `feature/issue-42-x` with `tiers.push` and `tiers.prCreate` set to `journal`. In the output, `tg` is the tier-gate decision (`ask`, or `allow` when it prints nothing), `bum` is block-unchecked-merge's exit code and `bd` is block-destructive's. Merge checks used a gh stub that reports green checks.
### P1 — Critical (Blocks Merge)
| **F1 · regression · `hooks/scripts/lib/command-parse.sh:713-714,762-788,823`; `hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:2162,1579`**<br>A pipe into a subshell, a group or a compound command no longer asks. Bash feeds the pipe to every command inside that `(...)`, `{...}`, `if`, `for` or `case`. The parser marks only the first simple command after the `\|` as piped. For `\| (bash)` that is the empty piece before `(`, which uses up the mark. `;` and each new nesting level also reset the mark. The tier gate now requires `TG_PIPED=1` before it treats a shell as reading its input, so the shell inside the group is not flagged.<br>Repro: `p.sh -c "echo 'gh pr merge 1' \| (bash)"`. **Old: `tg=ask`. New: `tg=allow`.** These behave the same way: `\| ( cd /tmp && bash )`, `\| (true; bash)`, `\| { true; bash; }`, `printf 'x\ngh pr merge 1\n' \| { read -r x; bash; }`, `\| if true; then bash; fi`, `\| case x in x) bash ;; esac`, `\| for i in 1; do bash; done`, `gh pr view 1 \| (cat; bash)`. In every case a merge runs with no prompt. Expected: ask, as before.<br>The new `tg-shell-argument` scenario in `tests/e2e-tier-gate.test.sh` has no row of this kind, so it passes with the regression in place. _(HIGH)_ | Carry the pipe mark into a level opened right after a pipe, and keep it across `;`, `&&` and `\|\|` until that `(`, `{` or compound keyword closes. Asking too often is the safe direction here. Add rows such as `shell\|echo x \| (bash); gh pr list` and `shell\|echo x \| { true; bash; }; gh pr list`. |
### P2 — Should Fix
| **F2 · regression · `hooks/scripts/lib/command-parse.sh:548-553`; `hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:543-566`**<br>There is a new false Tier 3 ask on ordinary heredocs whose introducer is followed by a pipe or a redirection. When the parser re-reads the command with heredoc bodies removed, it only removes a body whose `<<EOF` ends the line. Any other body stays in that reading, so `_tg_body_line` treats a lone-variable body line as a command. The old code exempted every kept body (`TG_KEPT`).<br>Repro: a command whose first line is `cat <<EOF \| gh pr create --title t --body-file -` and whose body holds a line `$SUMMARY`. **Old: allow (journaled). New: ask**, with the reason "...may merge a pull request or create a release... Command: $SUMMARY". The same happens with `cat <<EOF > body.md`, `cat <<EOF >&2`, and `gh pr comment 5 --body-file - <<'EOF' >/dev/null`. In the last one the body is quoted and never expanded, so it cannot run anything. `cat > body.md <<EOF` stays silent. Expected: silent, because the reader is not a shell. The documentation claims "data only in a non-shell reader's body", which these commands contradict. _(HIGH)_ | When `blank=1`, accept an introducer followed by redirections or a pipe, as long as nothing after it on the line is a shell or interpreter (run `reader_ok` on the whole line). Add the four commands above as `silent` rows. |
| **F3 · correctness (claim not met) · `hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:2205-2209`; `hooks/scripts/block-unchecked-merge.sh:117-124`**<br>The change claims that a word glued to a substitution is read again without it "in all three hooks". In the tier gate and the merge gate, the quick text check runs first, on the raw text. If the substitution splits the keyword itself, the text no longer contains `push`, `merge`, `release` or `gh`, and the hook exits before the second reading is made.<br>Repro: `git pu$(true)sh --tags` (a tag push, Tier 3), `g$(true)h rel$(true)ease create v9`, and `g$(true)h pr mer$(true)ge 7 --repo o/r --squash --admin`: tier gate allows all of them in both trees. For `gh pr mer$(true)ge 7` the tier gate asks, but the merge gate exits 0 in both trees (expected 2, a refusal). block-destructive does handle the mid-word form (`git res$(true)et --hard` → `bd=2`), so the two other hooks are inconsistent with it. This is not a regression, but the fix this change claims does not hold for this shape. _(HIGH)_ | Run the quick text check on the text with substitutions removed, or skip it when the text contains `$(` or a backquote. Add rows like `merge\|gh pr mer$(true)ge 1` and `release\|git pu$(true)sh --tags` (tier gate), and `gh pr mer$(true)ge 7` (merge gate). |
| **F4 · security · pre-existing · `hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:1543-1546` (the quoted-word exemption this change rewrote)**<br>A command word that is one quoted variable is exempt on the grounds that it is "one program name". When a pipe feeds it, that program can be a shell reading the piped text.<br>Repro: `SH=bash; echo 'gh pr merge 1' \| "$SH"` and `... \| "$SH" -s` are allowed in both trees. `\| $SH` (unquoted) asks. The new `TG_PIPED` flag already provides what is needed to close this. _(HIGH)_ | When `TG_PIPED=1` and the input is not redirected, treat a command word that cannot be read (quoted or not) as a possible shell and ask. Add `SH=bash; echo 'gh pr merge 1' \| "$SH"` as a `shell` row. |
### P3 — Consider
| **F5 · regression · `hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:569-577`**<br>`_tg_eval_read_by_name` matches its pattern against the raw command text, so a redirection after the eval breaks the match. The old check read the words, with redirections set aside.<br>Repro: `n=PR; eval "v=\${$n}" >/dev/null; gh pr view 1`. **Old: allow. New: ask.** _(HIGH)_ | Remove the redirections (the parser's `BD_RDIR` list) before matching, or match on the words. |
| **F6 · tests · `tests/e2e-tier-gate.test.sh` (tg-command-word, the `<<<` loop)**<br>The row `cat <<< EOF\ngh pr merge 1\nEOF` already asked at 45de0559, because a space after `<<` never matched the old heredoc pattern. It would still pass with the fix reverted. The `<<<EOF` and `<<<'EOF'` rows do catch a revert (old: allow, new: ask). _(HIGH)_ | Replace that row with one only the fix can pass, for example `cat <<<"EOF"`. |
| **F7 · security · pre-existing · `hooks/scripts/lib/command-parse.sh:900-906`**<br>The pass that reads text piped into a shell only starts when a shell's name appears in the raw text after the first `\|`. A backslash inside the name defeats that. `echo 'git reset --hard' \| bas\h` gives `bd=0` in both trees. `b\ash` is caught only because it ends in `ash`. _(HIGH)_ | Remove backslashes and quotes from the text before testing it against `_BD_SHELL_RE`. |
### Summary
